manifest.name: @aiwayds/dsh-subagent-registry
manifest.description: dsh plugin: register locally-defined custom agents (~/.dsh/agents/*.md) as callable subagents via the use_agent tool, with continuable background dispatch, ask_agent follow-ups, the /registry-config management command, and the opt-in codemode (jev + store) PTC toolchain

scripts.test: node test/deep-semantics.test.mjs && node test/display-name.test.mjs && node test/resume.test.mjs && node test/thinking-level.test.mjs && node test/agent-options.test.mjs && node test/interactive.test.mjs && node test/apply-smoke.test.mj...

manifest.author: fliu56

bundle.text:
# dsh-subagent-registry bundle patch: mounts the plugin into the profile's
# assembly tree under the stable plugin id `dsh-subagent-registry`. At startup
# it registers the `use_agent` tool, which lets the main-conversation model
# call any locally-defined custom agent (~/.dsh/agents/<name>.md) by name as a
# subagent through the already-assembled `spawn` subagent provider.
#
# Since 0.18.0 this package also carries the former @aiwayds/dsh-ptc-subagent
# toolchain: the `codemode` tool (jev decision binding + session-scoped store
# binding over the public ctx.ptcRuntime seam) registers ONLY when the entry
# config `ptcEnabled: true` is set (default false — the rows below stay inert
# for everyone who never opts in).
#
# Mounting convention: every @aiwayds bundle inserts its own main plugin here
# (dsh-tui mounts as `dsh-tui`, dsh-model-sync as `dsh-model-sync`, …) — a
# bundle main is NOT auto-mounted by the host, and without this row the
# `use_agent` tool never reaches the tool registry.
#
# Agent-preset support, since 0.19.1 (issue #9): the two SERVICE rows this
# patch used to carry (`agent-preset-registry` with `default: native` and
# `subagent-model-selection-settings`) are gone from the static patch. On a
# profile that also selects @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app the web-app inserts rows
# with the same ids, and a same-id insert from a later patch layer silently
# REPLACES the earlier row wholesale (the loader does not reject duplicated
# ids — it merges by id, last writer wins) — that both flipped the web
# profile's default preset from `standard` to our `native` and made
# `dsh plugin remove` refuse forever with `bundle-in-use` (the manager
# matches its bundle-in-use check against any live entry whose id and name
# appear in this patch file). The plugin now mounts both rows at runtime on
# the include tree, only when no same-id entry exists (src/preset-mount.ts) —
# so tui/headless profiles get exactly the layer they always had, and
# web/desktop profiles keep the web-app's own rows untouched. The two PRESET
# rows below stay static but carry a `disabled` guard: they only mount where
# no @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app bundle supplies its own preset roster, because
# unlike the service rows they would ADD a `Native`/`Codemode` entry to the
# web preset picker rather than collide with it.
#
# Known 0.2.0-rc.2 limitation (carried over from the ptc patch, verified on a
# real TUI): preset-level `tool-presentation mode: ptc` does not reach the
# wire — the `mode: ptc` row inside `preset-codemode` is kept for the day
# upstream fixes presentAs preset scoping, and is inert until then; the
# specialist persona is written for native tools + the codemode runner and
# does not assume `run_code`.

- insert:
    - id: dsh-subagent-registry
      name: '@aiwayds/dsh-subagent-registry'
      # Optional explicit config (every key has a schema default):
      #   agentsDir: ~/.dsh/agents     # agent files ($DSH_HOME-resolved default literal)
      #   provider: spawn              # subagent provider (dsh-base spawn)
      #   toolName: use_agent          # dispatch tool name
      #   askToolName: ask_agent       # follow-up tool name
      #   leafDenyTools: []            # deep:0 leaf deny list override
      #   resume: auto                 # auto | opt-in | off
      #   language: zh                 # zh | en | ru
      #   disabledAgents: []           # roster toggle — agent names excluded from the roster
      #   ptcEnabled: false            # opt-in: register the codemode (jev + store) tool
      #   jevEnabled: false            # jev master switch (default off: zero jev calls)
      #   jevBackend: zen              # zen | native | openrouter
      #   jevModel: ''                 # pinned model id; '' = backend default at call time
      #   jevTimeoutMs: 3000           # per-classify deadline, one signal, no retry
      #   jevSecretFile: ''            # outbound secret-gate literal list (one per line)
      #   storageDir: ''               # usage-sink dir; '' = <dsh home>/storages/ptc-subagent
    # The tui profile stack (and any profile without dsh-web-app) ships no
    # agent-preset layer, so the package mounts the registry itself. The two
    # service rows migrated from the @aiwayds/dsh-ptc-subagent patch are
    # mounted at runtime by src/preset-mount.ts (issue #9 — see the header);
    # this file deliberately does NOT declare them. Proven on a real TUI
    # (2026-10-14): without the support layer the preset silently fails to
    # mount — `preset-native` (empty plugins, `default: native`) shadows no
    # ambient row, so sessions that never pick a preset compose exactly as
    # before; `model-selection-settings` is the host-scope service the
    # official preset's `modelSelection: true` rows require.
    #
    # The two preset rows below stay patch-level, guarded: the `disabled`
    # expression evaluates per-entry at mount time against the loader context
    # (same seam the web-app's own patch uses for its desktop-only rows) and
    # disables both rows on any profile whose selected bundles include
    # @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app — that bundle ships its own preset roster
    # (standard/ptc/minimal), and a second, colliding roster would only add
    # noise to the web preset picker. On every other profile the expression
    # is false and the rows mount exactly as before the guard.
    - id: preset-native
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      disabled: !!js "ctx.get('profileContext')?.startedBundles?.includes('@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app') ?? false"
      config:
        id: native
        name: Native
        description: Ambient composition - no preset rows; the pre-preset native face.
        order: 0
        plugins:
          - id: tool-presentation
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-tool-presentation'
            config:
              mode: native
    # The Codemode preset (migrated from @aiwayds/dsh-ptc-subagent): the
    # official PTC preset rows + a specialist persona. Only meaningful once
    # `ptcEnabled: true` puts the codemode tool on the registry — the persona
    # below is the same text the opt-in `ptc-subagent` agent template ships,
    # so sessions that pick this preset and dispatch the specialist behave
    # identically.
    - id: preset-codemode
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      disabled: !!js "ctx.get('profileContext')?.startedBundles?.includes('@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app') ?? false"
      config:
        id: codemode
        name: Codemode
        description: Dedicated PTC subagent for batch classification/evaluation/aggregation — codemode programs over the jev decision backend and the session-scoped store.
        order: 3
        plugins:
          - id: persona
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              prefix: |
                You are the decision-work subagent of a DeepSeek Harness session. Your one job is batch work: classify item sets, score candidates against rubrics, answer yes/no questions with calibrated judgment, and aggregate results into structured JSON. You are dispatched by the main agent; do the dispatched batch work and return the aggregate — do not chat, explore repositories on your own, or take over the session's goals.

                Division of labor: your native tools (read, bash, fs search, and friends) gather and write the data; the codemode tool runs your decision programs. A codemode program is an async TypeScript body — top-level await/return are available, the return value must be lossless JSON, and Promise.all is the fan-out primitive. Read the input with your native tools, pass compact per-item states into the program, and write the aggregate back out (or return it directly) when the dispatch asks for a file:

                    const verdicts = await Promise.all(items.map((item) => jev.classify({
                      questions: {
                        relevance: { type: 'choice', criteria: { on_topic: 'about the query', off_topic: 'unrelated' } },
                        quality: { type: 'score', criteria: ['Poor — unusable', 'Fair — needs work', 'Good — minor gaps', 'Excellent — ship it'] },
                        approve: { type: 'noul', criteria: { true: 'ready as-is', false: 'needs another pass' } },
                      },
                      state: JSON.stringify(item),
                    })))
                    return { approved: verdicts.filter((v) => v.answers.approve.value > 0.8).length, total: items.length }

                jev question types. `choice`: criteria is a map of option name → description; the answer carries the selected key plus per-option probabilities. `score`: criteria is an ordered list of level names (the text before " — " is the canonical level); the answer is a numeric position on that spectrum, and may land between levels. `noul`: criteria is two-sided { true, false } (single-sided criteria measurably degrade calibration); the answer is one 0..1 probability — mid-range values are UNCERTAINTY, threshold only the high segment. Each classify is ONE batched round trip: pack every question about a state into a single call, never one call per question.

                jev.classify never rejects. Failures resolve a structured { error, message } — 'disabled' (the decision layer is off: fall back to your own judgment and say so in the result), 'no-key', 'timeout', 'http' (carries the status), 'invalid-response'. Probe once per program with jev.isConfigured() and branch. Every call is logged with its spend; the run result reports jevCalls metadata — keep an eye on it and prefer fewer, batched calls.

                store is session-scoped key/value memory: await store.store(key, value) and await store.load(key). It rides the session's durable log, so it survives resume and is fork-separated — this branch only ever sees its own path's writes. Quotas: 256KB per value, 1MB per branch state; an over-quota write fails with a structured error explaining that bulk data belongs in files (use your native file tools), not in store.

                A failed codemode run comes back as CODE_RUN_FAILED carrying the failure kind and your captured logs: read them, fix the program, and rerun — failures are self-correction fuel, not dead ends.
              # No persona suffix: the old `Your working directory is {{cwd}}.`
              # referenced a prompt variable no host generation registers (the
              # agent loop registers only provider/model, on 0.2.1-rc.x and
              # 0.2.2+ alike), and strict prompt interpolation rejects unknown
              # variables at assembly — the suffix killed the first turn of
              # every codemode session (issue #8, second finding). The working
              # directory still reaches the model through the
              # working-directory:current runtime context
              # (dsh-working-directory, interpolate: false) that the persona
              # includes by default (includeRuntimeContext: true).
          - id: agent-instructions
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
            config:
              maxBytes: 65536
          - id: tool-bash
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash'
            disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'
          - id: tool-pwsh
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh'
            disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'
          - id: tool-fs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'
          - id: tool-fs-search
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search'
            config:
              sampleOverCapGlobResults: false
          - id: tool-jobs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs'
          - id: skill-filesystem
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
          - id: tool-skill
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'
          - id: command-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-goal'
          - id: tool-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal'
          - id: planning
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              planMode: true
            config:
              - id: plan-mode
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode'
                config:
                  section: |
                    You are in plan mode. Stay in plan mode until exit_plan_mode succeeds or the user switches the session mode. Imperative language to implement changes means plan the implementation, not execute it. A user's conversational agreement — including an answer confirming something you asked — approves nothing and does not end plan mode; fold the confirmed decision into the plan and submit it through exit_plan_mode.

                    Explore first. Use non-mutating reads, searches, static analysis, and checks to ground the plan in the actual repository. Do not edit or write files, change configuration, run formatters or code generation that rewrites tracked files, commit, or otherwise carry out the plan. Prefer existing functions and patterns over new machinery.

                    The tool catalog stays the same across modes for request-cache stability. These plan-mode rules override any later tool description or guidance that suggests using mutation tools; those tools remain listed to keep the tool catalog unchanged. Do not use todo_write to track this planning phase: it tracks implementation after an approved plan, while the plan itself belongs in exit_plan_mode.

                    Resolve discoverable facts by inspection. Use ask_user_question only for user-owned choices or material ambiguity that inspection cannot answer. Do not ask the user where code lives or how current behavior works when you can find out.

                    Make the plan decision-complete: state the goal and success criteria; group implementation changes by subsystem; identify public API, schema, and data-flow changes; cover edge cases, failure modes, tests, acceptance criteria, and explicit assumptions. Keep it concise enough to review but detailed enough that another engineer can implement it without making design decisions.

                    When ready, call exit_plan_mode with the complete plan markdown, starting with a # title. Make exit_plan_mode the only and final tool call in that assistant response: it presents the plan for approval, and implementation begins only in a later step after approval. Do not paste the final plan as a plain reply or ask "should I proceed?" through prose or ask_user_question. If review rejects it, incorporate the feedback and present again. If the review channel is unavailable or aborted, stay in plan mode and ask the user to switch modes manually; do not proceed with implementation.
          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
              toolResultPruner: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'
              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'
              - id: tool-result-pruner
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
                config:
                  thresholdChars: 8192
                  headChars: 4096
                  tailChars: 1024
          - id: delegation
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              workflowEngine: true
            config:
              - id: tool-subagent-control
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'
              # list_agents mount rides a per-host bridge (fixes #8): upstream
              # removed the ./list-agents subpath from the control package's
              # exports map in 0.2.2 (its main entry now registers discovery
              # itself), so importing that subpath directly fails the whole
              # preset with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED / never started on
              # 0.2.2+ hosts. The bridge inspects the installed control
              # package's exports map and imports the legacy sub-entry only
              # where it still exists (0.2.0-rc.2 … 0.2.1-rc.x), keeping
              # exactly one registration on every generation.
              - id: tool-subagent-list-agents
                name: '@aiwayds/dsh-subagent-registry/legacy-subagent-list-agents'
              - id: tool-subagent
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: subagent
                  modelSelection: true
              - id: tool-subagent-fork
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: fork
                  toolName: subagent_fork
              - id: tool-subagent-codex
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                disabled: true
                config:
                  provider: codex
                  toolName: subagent_codex
                  maxDepth: provider-managed
              - id: tool-subagent-claude-code
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                disabled: true
                config:
                  provider: claude-code
                  toolName: subagent_claude_code
                  maxDepth: provider-managed
              - id: workflow-ptc
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-ptc'
                disabled: true
                config:
                  provider: spawn
              - id: tool-workflow
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-workflow'
                disabled: true
              - id: tool-ralph
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ralph'
                disabled: true
                config:
                  subagentProvider: spawn
                  maxRounds: 64
          - id: tool-ask-user
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'
          - id: tool-todo
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
            config:
              allowParallelInProgress: true
          - id: tool-web
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
            config:
              fetch: true
              searchTimeoutMs: 60000
          - id: tool-presentation
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-tool-presentation'
            config:
              mode: ptc
          - id: present
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-present'
          - id: tool-plugin-manager
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-manager/tools'
            disabled: true

readme.text:
[English](./README.en.md)

把 `~/.dsh/agents/*.md` 定义的自定义 agent（frontmatter 元数据 + markdown
正文作为 persona/system prompt）注册成 [dsh](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
可按名调用的 subagent：主对话通过 `use_agent` 点名调用，`ask_agent` 对后台
代理追问并等回复。跑在 dsh 自带的 `spawn` provider 上，纯插件、不改 dsh 本体。

- **一个 markdown 文件就是一个 agent** — frontmatter 写模型/思考强度，正文就是
  system prompt，改完即生效。
- **断点续跑** — 长任务中断（报错/取消/限额/崩溃）后再次调用，自动从已保存的
  中间进度继续，不从头重来。
- **按角色优先委派** — 使用精简英文委派指导，要求选择名册中匹配的自定义角色并提供完整任务上下文；独立任务后台并行，仅在必须继承当前对话时使用 `subagent_fork`。指导只在当前作用域可见本插件工具时生效，卸载后恢复官方指导。
- **后台派发 + 双向追问** — `background: true` 把代理放到后台跑，主对话继续干活；
  `ask_agent` 发追问并等它的回复。
- **开箱即用三个人物** — 装好即自动植入 `workhorse` / `oldfox` / `rubber-duck`
  三个预置 agent（见下）。
- **/registry-config 管理命令** — 向导式停用/启用任意名册 agent（`disabledAgents`
  配置键过滤，永不碰 md 文件）、安装两个 opt-in agent、联动 codemode 工具链
  开关（见下）。
- **opt-in PTC 能力** — 0.18.0 并入 `@aiwayds/dsh-ptc-subagent` 全部代码：
  `codemode` 工具（jev 判定 + 会话级 store）按 `ptcEnabled` 门控注册，默认
  完全关闭（见下）。
- **⚠️ Experimental（试验性功能，默认关闭）** — `ptc-subagent` /
  `minimal-subagent` 两个 opt-in agent 与整条 codemode（PTC）工具链都属试验性
  产品面：能力已迁移合并，但默认一律关闭，仅经 `/registry-config` 显式勾选或
  `ptcEnabled` 等配置键显式开启后才生效（见下）。
- **站在官方 subagent 机制之上** — 不自建执行器：每个自定义 agent 都通过 dsh
  官方的 `spawn` provider 启动，子代理就是货真价实的 dsh subagent（完整会话、
  持久化、continuable）。官方 subagent 栈的新能力（如双向通信）本插件自动
  继承；官方原生 `subagent` 工具继续可用，两者并存、互不干扰。
- **纯插件** — 支持 DSH RC/稳定线的公开 subagent 机制（兼容性验证至 `0.2.0-rc.2` 与 `0.2.1-rc.2`），可随时干净卸载；alpha 线不再支持。

按宿主公开 API 自动选择派发方式（功能探测，无版本号分支）：0.2.1 线使用 `startActivation`，前台/后台分别以 `caller` / `parent` 投递；0.2.0 线使用 `start` / `startContinuable`。已选择的接口失败后直接报错，不尝试另一接口重复派发。0.2.1 线的启动请求不再携带 persona 与 leaf 工具限制——本插件在 `subagent/start` 边缘把预留的 persona 段与 leaf 工具限制安装到子代理自身作用域（宿主自身合成同一窗口的同一 section/restrict），语义与 0.2.0 线的请求字段一致。前台续跑使用公开 `agents.resume`，支持当前 persona/model/工具配置及调用取消，但不占用 manager 并发槽，也不能由 `interrupt_agent` 打断；续跑子代理不能使用 stock `send_message` 联系父级。后台追问继续由 manager 管理。已选中的旧会话若读取或恢复失败，会报错；显式 `fresh: true` 才重新派发。

readme.section: 三个预置 agent（三件套种子）+ 两个 opt-in
readme.text:
首次启动时植入 `~/.dsh/agents/`（仅当目录里还没有可解析的 agent 时；你的修改
永远不会被覆盖）。它们就是普通的 markdown 文件，随便改。

| Agent | 一句话 | 典型用法 |
| ----- | ------ | -------- |
| **workhorse**（牛马狗） | 干活的主力：写代码、调查、测试、部署，脏活累活全包；默认 `deepseek-flash`，受保护禁止危险操作 | 「用 workhorse 把发布清单整理成表格」 |
| **oldfox**（老法师） | 顾问不干活：分析、trouble shooting、review 挑刺，只把关不动手；`glm-5.3` | 「让 oldfox 审一下这个方案」 |
| **rubber-duck**（小黄鸭） | 多模态视觉 agent：看截图/图表/手写字，画 plotext/mermaid/matplotlib 图；跑在支持图像的模型上 | 「用 rubber-duck 看这个截图，提取页面文字」 |

readme.section: 三个预置 agent（三件套种子）+ 两个 opt-in
readme.text:
另有**两个 opt-in agent**（默认不装）：
⚠️ **Experimental — disabled by default（试验性功能，默认关闭）**。
`ptc-subagent`（批量判定专员，联动 codemode 工具链）与 `minimal-subagent`
（极简终端执行器，叶子）——能力已迁移合并，但产品面仍属试验阶段，默认关闭，
仅经 `/registry-config` 命令显式勾选（或手工拷贝包内
`templates/opt-in-agents/<语言>/<名字>.md` 并写配置键）后启用；已有文件不
覆盖，取消勾选不删除。种子只撒三件套——opt-in 永不自动安装。

装好、重启 dsh，然后在对话里直接说——主模型会按名字挑 agent：

> 用 workhorse 把今天的发布清单整理成表格

底层就是 `use_agent(agent: "workhorse", prompt: "…")`。后台代理用
`ask_agent(agent: "worker", message: "…")` 追问，会等它的回复。

在 Web 左侧主导航栏选择 **子智能体**，进入主工作区的完整管理页。页面自动读取实际 `agentsDir`，支持新增、复制、编辑、原文修复和删除；错误文件保留诊断，不会因刷新空目录而补文件。内部名称创建后固定；显示名变更前确认历史按名续跑或追问的影响。

管理页成功保存、删除、打开或刷新后，后续模型请求的工具名册即时更新，正在运行的调用保持原有 persona。手工改文件后打开管理页或刷新即可同步名册；纯 CLI/TUI 仍按次读取角色，静态名册在下次挂载时更新。

保存检测外部修改并保留未知字段、注释及未编辑正文；不能安全局部更新的文件转原文编辑。取消自身放弃/刷新确认或保存失败时保留草稿。切到宿主其他页再回来仍可继续本客户端草稿，重启或卸载不保证恢复。目录可能被多个 profile 共享，删除需确认此影响。

本次客户端包需要重新构建和安装；已有进程若未重载插件需重启以加载新的客户端入口。加载入口后，预设 CRUD 本身不需要重启。

往 `~/.dsh/agents/` 丢一个文件：

```markdown
---
name: my-agent
description: "一行简介，显示在 use_agent 名册里"
model: opencode-go/deepseek-flash

Frontmatter 字段：`name`（必填）、`description`、`display_name`、`model`
（`provider/model`，缺省继承）、`thinking`（`off/low/medium/high/max`，缺省继承）、
`deep`（`0` = 叶子不许再开子代理，缺省 `1`）、`background`（`true` = 默认后台跑）、`maxRounds`（正整数，per-agent 轮数上限，覆盖 `dsh-tui.maxRounds` 全局值；宿主 TUI 的硬停梯消费）。
未知字段静默忽略。

readme.section: 并发与轮数上限（0.1.7 起）
readme.text:
**并发数与嵌套深度由官方 dsh-subagent 托管**，本插件不自管并发计数与排队
（官方 ActivationManager 统一调度）：`maxActiveSubagents`（同时活跃子代理上限，
默认 `8`）与 `maxDepth`（委托嵌套深度上限，默认 `1`）。两者都是 volatile 字段，
免重启热调——在 profile patch 里写 `subagent: { maxActiveSubagents: N, maxDepth: M }`，
或运行时 `settings.update('subagent', …)`。`use_agent` 的 `deep` frontmatter
只是在这条官方深度预算内再收紧（`deep: 0` 叶子直接拔掉所有开代理的工具）。

`maxRounds`（per-agent 轮数上限）**本插件继续保留**：官方 subagent seam 没有轮数
预算能力，该键仍由宿主 TUI 的硬停梯消费。

readme.section: 并发与轮数上限（0.1.7 起）
readme.text:
→ **完整参考**：[docs/AGENT-FORMAT.md](./docs/AGENT-FORMAT.md)（英文）——每个字段
的校验与失败行为、`deep`/`thinking` 语义、续跑机制、后台派发、配置项、已知边界。

| 键              | 默认            | 说明                                                                                             |
| --------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `agentsDir`     | `~/.dsh/agents` | agent 文件目录；默认字面量按 `$DSH_HOME` 解析，自定义值展开 `~` 后原样使用。                       |
| `provider`      | `spawn`         | 子代理 provider（复用 dsh-base 的 spawn）。                                                       |
| `toolName`      | `use_agent`     | 派发工具名。                                                                                      |
| `askToolName`   | `ask_agent`     | 追问工具名。                                                                                      |
| `leafDenyTools` | `[]`            | `deep: 0` 叶子子的禁用工具表；空 = 静态默认再与宿主已注册工具取交集。                              |
| `resume`        | `auto`          | 续跑档位：`auto` / `opt-in` / `off`。                                                             |
| `language`      | `zh`            | 界面语言：`zh`（中文，默认）/ `en`（English）/ `ru`（Русский）。作用于 web 管理面板文案、内置技能正文与模型路由描述、首次播种的预置 agent 模板（`templates/agents/<language>/`）；改后重启 dsh 生效，已存在的 ag

会话里输入 `/registry-config` 打开管理向导（ask_user_question 两道多选题）：

1. **停用开关**：勾选要停用的 agent（勾选集合 = 新的 `disabledAgents`；不勾 =
   全部启用；已停用的名字要**保持勾选**才继续停用，选项描述标注当前状态）。
   开关作用域覆盖名册全部 agent（含你自己定义的），**永不碰任何 md 文件**。
2. **opt-in 安装**：勾选 `ptc-subagent` / `minimal-subagent` 安装可选 agent
   （⚠️ Experimental 试验性功能，默认关闭）。拷模板、已有不覆盖、取消勾选不
   删除；选 ptc 联动 `ptcEnabled: true` +
   拷 md；取消选联动反向（写 false + 把 ptc-subagent 停用进 `disabledAgents`，
   已拷 md 保留不删）。

生效时机：`disabledAgents` 是 volatile 键，命令收尾自动刷新名册、立即生效；
`ptcEnabled` 变更要等插件下次挂载（重启 dsh）。无头部署没有 ask 面板（ask 报
NO_PROVIDER）时，命令降级为错误文案，指引用手改配置键（`disabledAgents` /
`ptcEnabled` + 手工拷 `templates/opt-in-agents/<语言>/<名字>.md`）。

> ⚠️ **Experimental — disabled by default（试验性功能，默认关闭）**：能力已
> 迁移合并，产品面仍属试验阶段；`ptcEnabled: false`（默认）不注册任何工具。

0.18.0 起本插件并入了原 `@aiwayds/dsh-ptc-subagent` 的全部代码：`codemode`
工具是一台插件自有的 PTC runner——异步 TypeScript 程序体跑在公开
`ctx.ptcRuntime` seam 上，带一对为批量工作造的绑定：**`jev`**（校准判定后端，
`classify` 一次往返判成批 choice/score/noul 问题，失败返回结构化 `{error}`
而绝不 reject；1:1 直通 `@aiwayds/dsh-jev-core`）与 **`store`**（会话级键值
记忆，挂在会话持久日志上——resume 后仍在、按 fork 隔离，配额 256KB/值、
1MB/分支）。失败的 run 以宿主自身的 `CODE_RUN_FAILED` 合同返回（失败类别 +
捕获日志），结果报告 `{value, logs, jevCalls, storeWrites}`。

- **默认完全关闭**：`ptcEnabled: false` 不注册工具；`jevEnabled: false` 零
  jev 调用。每次 jev 调用（含失败）在
  `<dsh home>/storages/ptc-subagent/usage.jsonl` 落一行（只记元数据与 token
  数，永记状态文本）。
- **配套**：`ptc-subagent` opt-in 模板是专职派发角色；自 0.19.1 起 bundle patch
  只保留两条带守卫的 preset 行（`preset-native` / `preset-codemode`，在选择
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` 的 profile 上自动禁用），两条服务行
  （`agent-preset-registry` / `subagent-model-selection-settings`）改为插件启动时
  在 include 树上运行时挂载、仅在树上没有同 id 条目时创建——已挂 agent-preset
  层的 profile 无需手动去重（issue #9，见 docs/TROUBLESHOOTING-PRESET-ROWS.md）。
- **升级自独立 ptc 仓**：用法与配置键同名同义（entry id 换成
  `dsh-subagent-registry`），usage.jsonl 落盘路径不变，历史记录直接延续。

插件随包注册一个名为 `dsh-subagent-registry-config` 的技能（bundled skill）。对话涉及自定义
子代理、agent `.md` 编写、子代理续跑或本插件配置时，dsh 会自动加载这份使用与配置指南，
主模型可以据此用 `ask_user_question` 代写 agent 文件、调整插件配置，无需翻 README。
技能与插件同版本发布，随 npm 包携带（`skills/dsh-subagent-registry-config/SKILL.md`，
另有英文版 `SKILL.en.md` 与俄文版 `SKILL.ru.md`，由 `language` 键选择，见上表）。

**要求 dsh >= 0.2.0-rc.2**（RC/稳定线；alpha 线不再支持）。兼容性验证至 `0.2.0-rc.2` 与 `0.2.1-rc.2`。宿主须挂载会话持久化及 `sessionQuery` 服务；续跑与追问使用各版本自身的会话格式，不提供跨版本迁移。

方式 A — 把本地 checkout 挂进 dsh profile：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile tui add ~/github/dsh-subagent-registry
```

方式 B — npm 依赖：`npm i @aiwayds/dsh-subagent-registry`，然后在 profile
配置里以稳定 id `dsh-subagent-registry` 加载，或通过 bundle patch 挂载
（挂法见本仓 `cordis.patch.yml`）。

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> remove @aiwayds/dsh-subagent-registry
```

宿主会把插件从 profile 里摘除；重启 dsh 后 `use_agent` / `ask_agent` 工具
消失。**`~/.dsh/agents/` 里的 agent 文件会保留**——它们归你所有，不会被
重新植入或覆盖。没有本插件时 dsh-tui-pi 会优雅降级（只是失去自定义 agent
派发能力）。

```sh
npm run check    # tsc --noEmit
npm run build    # tsc -> lib/
npm test         # 单元回归及临时目录中的真实 npm 安装检查（无 LLM）
npm run test:host # 当前 SDK 的真实服务/持久化/manager/spawn；脚本化模型，无网络

从插件目录初始化隔离 SDK（已有环境无需重复安装）：

```sh
npm install --prefix ../../.tmp/dsh-type-closure-rc2 --ignore-scripts @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query@0.2.0-rc.2
npm install --prefix ../../.tmp/dsh-type-closure --ignore-scripts @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.2 @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query@0.2.1-rc.2 @deepseek-ai/dsh-working-directory@0.2.1-rc.2
```

可用 `DSH_TEST_RC2_CLOSURE_DIR` / `DSH_TEST_021_CLOSURE_DIR` 指向其他隔离环境的 `node_modules`；测试只将模型脚本化，服务与持久化使用对应版本的真实实现。

readme.section: `@deepseek-ai/*` 依赖契约（为什么是 optional peer）
readme.text:
本仓对 `@deepseek-ai/*`（`cordis`、`dsh-subagent`、`dsh-llm`、`schemastery` 等）
在发布包中声明 **optional peerDependencies**（`>=0.2.0-rc.2 || >=0.2.1-rc.1`）。这是有意的两层分工：

readme.section: `@deepseek-ai/*` 依赖契约（为什么是 optional peer）
readme.text:
- **发布语义（给消费者）**：声明表达「使用宿主自带的同名包、版本下限
  `>=0.2.0-rc.2 || >=0.2.1-rc.1`」。optional peer 不会被 pnpm / npm 自动安装，因此不会在
  profile 的 `node_modules` 里生成第二份拷贝去遮蔽（shadow）宿主 bundled 的
  闭包。会出事的是硬 dependency 精确钉旧 rc 版——那会把宿主 0.2.x 弄到无法
  boot（已知社区事故模式）。
- **开发 typecheck（给本仓）**：devDependencies 钉住新版 SDK，`scripts/link-dsh-closure.mjs`
  （postinstall）把 `node_modules/@deepseek-ai/*` 软链到 `DSH_CLOSURE_DIR` 指定或全局 dsh 安装的闭包，
  保证类型图里只有一份 `@deepseek-ai/cordis`——出现第二份会打断 cordis 的
  `declare module` 类型增强（`Property 'settings' does not exist on type
  'Context'`）。

readme.section: `@deepseek-ai/*` 依赖契约（为什么是 optional peer）
readme.text:
维护守则：这些包永远保持 optional peer 形态——不要移回 dependencies /
devDependencies，也不要去掉 `optional: true`（非 optional peer 在
`auto-install-peers` 开启的 pnpm 下会被自动安装，第二副本问题即复发）；同样不要新增任何硬 dependencies——钉死的第二份拷贝会以同样方式遮蔽宿主闭包。

`e2e/podman-install/` installs the **published** tarballs of this plugin, dsh-dcp, dsh-cron, dsh-llm-proxy, and dsh-profile-switch inside a container with a real dsh CLI, using a real npm client with dependency lifecycle scripts on — the exact intersection that let the packaged-`postinstall` breakage (#2) ship unnoticed. It asserts the install exits clean, the closure linker stands down in the consumer tree, the real host composes and boots each profile, and dcp's schema default + explicit-empty semantics survive the real config layer.

- Local (macOS, podman machine up): `e2e/podman-install/run.sh`
- The same assertions run bare on Linux (no podman needed) via the weekly scheduled `e2e install` workflow; `bash e2e/podman-install/entry.sh` works on any node 22+ machine with the global dsh CLI.
Apache-2.0

[中文](./README.md)

Register locally-defined custom agents (`~/.dsh/agents/*.md`) as callable
subagents in [dsh](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — the main
conversation invokes them by name through `use_agent`, background runs take
follow-ups via `ask_agent`, and interrupted runs resume from their saved
partial work. No host patching, no code — a markdown file per agent.

- **One markdown file is one agent** — frontmatter carries the model/thinking
  settings, the body is the system prompt, changes take effect immediately.
- **Resumes interrupted runs** — after an error, cancellation, token limit or
  crash, the next call for the same agent continues from the saved partial
  work instead of starting over.
- **Role-aware delegation guidance** — Concise English guidance directs delegation to a matching custom role with a self-contained prompt, runs independent tasks in the background, and uses `subagent_fork` only when conversation inheritance is necessary. It applies only where this plugin's dispatch tool is visible; unloading restores the host guidance.
- **Background dispatch + two-way follow-ups** — `background: true` runs the
  agent as a durable background conversation while the parent keeps working;
  `ask_agent` sends a follow-up and waits for the reply.
- **Three personas out of the box** — `workhorse` / `oldfox` / `rubber-duck`
  are seeded on first start (see below).
- **The /registry-config management command** — wizard-based enable/disable for any
  roster agent (a `disabledAgents` config-key filter that never touches md
  files), opt-in

Dispatch is selected by public API availability (feature detection, no version-number branches): the 0.2.1 line uses `startActivation` with `caller` / `parent` delivery for foreground/background work; the 0.2.0 line uses `start` / `startContinuable`. A selected call's failure is propagated without retrying through another dispatch API. On the 0.2.1 line the start request no longer carries a child persona or the leaf tool filter — the plugin installs the reserved persona section and leaf restriction on the child's own agent scope at the `subagent/start` edge (the same section and window the host's own composition uses), matching the 0.2.0-line request-field semantics. Foreground resume uses public `agents.resume` with current composition and caller cancellation, but is outside manager capacity and `interrupt_agent` control; resumed children cannot use stock `send_message` to contact the parent. Background follow-ups remain managed. Failure to inspect or resume a selected session is an error; use explicit `fresh: true` to restart.

readme.section: The three shipped agents (the seed trio) + two opt-ins
readme.text:
Seeded into `~/.dsh/agents/` on first start (only when the directory holds no
parsable agent — your edits are never overwritten). All three are ordinary
markdown files: edit them freely.

readme.section: The three shipped agents (the seed trio) + two opt-ins
readme.text:
| Agent | Role | Example |
| ----- | ---- | ------- |
| **workhorse** (牛马狗) | The workhorse: writes code, investigates, tests, deploys — all the grunt work; default `deepseek-flash`, guarded against dangerous operations | "Use workhorse to turn the release checklist into a table" |
| **oldfox** (老法师) | The advisor who doesn't build: analysis, trouble shooting, review, audits — checks, never implements; `glm-5.3` | "Have oldfox review this design" |
| **rubber-duck** (小黄鸭) | Multimodal visual agent: reads screenshots / charts / handwriting, draws plotext / mermaid / matplotlib figures; runs on an image-capable model | "Use rubber-duck on this screenshot, extract the page text" |

readme.section: The three shipped agents (the seed trio) + two opt-ins
readme.text:
Two **opt-in agents** ship alongside (not installed by default):
⚠️ **Experimental — disabled by default**. `ptc-subagent` (the batch
decision-work specialist; linked to the codemode toolchain) and
`minimal-subagent` (the terminal-only executor, a leaf) — the capability has
migrated and merged, but the product surface stays experimental until it
graduates: nothing is installed or enabled until you explicitly check them in
the `/registry-config` command (or copy
`templates/opt-in-agents/<language>/<name>.md` from the package by hand and
write the config keys); existing files are never overwritten, unchecking never
deletes. The seed is the trio only — opt-ins are never installed automatically.

Install, restart dsh, then just ask in the conversation — the main model picks
the agent by name:

> Use workhorse to turn today's release checklist into a table

Under the hood that is `use_agent(agent: "workhorse", prompt: "…")`. For
background runs, follow up with `ask_agent(agent: "worker", message: "…")` —
it waits for the reply.

Select **子智能体** in the left sidebar navigation to open a full workspace page. It reads the configured `agentsDir` and supports creating, copying, editing, repairing complete source, and deleting presets. Broken files keep their diagnostics; reading or refreshing an empty directory does not seed files. Existing internal names are fixed. Display-name changes require confirmation because older runs may no longer be found by name.

Opening, refreshing, saving, or deleting refreshes the roster for subsequent model requests without stopping running calls or changing their personas. After manual file edits, reopen or refresh the page. CLI/TUI dispatch still reads each role at invocation; without the Web manager its static roster updates on remount.

Updates preserve unknown fields, comments and untouched body text, reject external revisions, and use full source editing when local changes cannot be preserved safely. Failed saves and cancelled discard confirmations retain the draft. Switching host pages retains the current client's draft; restarting or unloading the plugin does not. Deletion confirms the impact on profiles sharing the directory.
Build and install the client artifact; an existing process may need a restart to load this new plugin entry. Once loaded, preset CRUD needs no restart.

Drop a file into `~/.dsh/agents/`:

```markdown
---
name: my-agent
description: "One-line subtitle shown in the use_agent roster"
model: opencode-go/deepseek-flash

Frontmatter keys: `name` (required), `description`, `display_name`, `model`
(`provider/model`; absent = inherit), `thinking`
(`off/low/medium/high/max`; absent = inherit), `deep` (`0` = leaf, may not
spawn subagents; default `1`), `background` (`true` = dispatch in the
background by default). Unknown keys are silently ignored.

**Concurrency and nesting depth are owned by the official dsh-subagent
service** — this plugin keeps no concurrency counter or queue of its own (the
official ActivationManager schedules): `maxActiveSubagents` (live-children
cap, default `8`) and `maxDepth` (delegation-depth cap, default `1`). Both are
volatile fields, tunable without a restart — via a profile patch
`subagent: { maxActiveSubagents: N, maxDepth: M }` or at runtime with
`settings.update('subagent', …)`. The `use_agent` `deep` frontmatter only
tightens within that official depth budget (`deep: 0` leaves strip every
agent-spawning tool outright).

`maxRounds` (a per-agent turn budget) **stays**: the official subagent seam
has no round-budget capability, and the key is still consumed by the host
TUI's hard-stop ladder.

→ **Full reference**: [docs/AGENT-FORMAT.md](docs/AGENT-FORMAT.md) — every key's
validation and failure modes, `deep`/`thinking` semantics, resume mechanics,
background dispatch, configuration fields, known limitations.

The config hangs on the patch mount block that loads the plugin (the `config:`
section of the cordis.patch.yml `insert` entry):

| Key             | Default         | Description                                                                                       |
| --------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `agentsDir`     | `~/.dsh/agents` | Agent file directory; the default literal is resolved against `$DSH_HOME`, custom values are used verbatim after `~` expansion. |
| `provider`      | `spawn`         | Subagent provider (reuses dsh-base's `spawn`).                                                    |
| `toolName`      | `use_agent`     | Dispatch tool name.                                                                               |
| `askToolName`   | `ask_agent`     | Follow-up tool name.                                                                              |
| `leafDenyTools` | `[]`            | Tool deny list for `deep: 0` leaf children; empty = static default intersected with the host's registered tools. |
| `resume`        | `auto`          | Resume mode: `auto` / `opt-in` / `off`.                                                           |
| `language`      | `zh`            | UI language:

Type `/registry-config` in the session to open the management wizard (two
multi-select questions through ask_user_question):

1. **The disable toggle**: check the agents to disable (the checked set
   becomes the new `disabledAgents`; nothing checked = all enabled; currently
   disabled names must STAY checked to remain disabled — option descriptions
   mark the current state). The scope covers every roster agent (including
   your own), and **no md file is ever touched**.
2. **Opt-in installs**: check `ptc-subagent` / `minimal-subagent` to install
   (⚠️ Experimental — disabled by default). Template copy; existing files
   never overwritten; unchecking never deletes. Selecting ptc links
   `ptcEnabled: true` and copies the md;
   unselecting links the reverse (writes false and parks ptc-subagent in
   `disabledAgents`, the copied md is kept).

Timing: `disabledAgents` is volatile — the command refreshes the roster at the
end, so it applies immediately; a `ptcEnabled` change waits for the next plugin
mount (dsh restart). On a headless deployment without an ask surface (the ask
rejects with NO_PROVIDER) the command degrades to an error message with the
manual recipe (the `disabledAgents` / `ptcEnabled` keys plus copying
`templates/opt-in-agents/<language>/<name>.md` by hand).

readme.section: The ptc capability (opt-in: the codemode tool)
readme.text:
> ⚠️ **Experimental — disabled by default**: the capability has migrated and
> merged, the product surface stays experimental; `ptcEnabled: false` (the
> default) registers no tool.

readme.section: The ptc capability (opt-in: the codemode tool)
readme.text:
Since 0.18.0 this package carries the entire former `@aiwayds/dsh-ptc-subagent`:
the `codemode` tool is a plugin-owned PTC runner — async TypeScript program
bodies over the public `ctx.ptcRuntime` seam, with a binding pair purpose-built
for batch work: **`jev`** (one calibrated decision backend; `classify` answers
a batched set of choice/score/noul questions in one round trip and resolves
structured `{error}` results instead of rejecting; a 1:1 passthrough to
`@aiwayds/dsh-jev-core`) and **`store`** (session-scoped key/value memory on
the durable session log — survives resume, fork-separated; 256KB per value,
1MB per branch). A failed run returns through the host's own `CODE_RUN_FAILED`
contract (failure kind + captured logs); the result reports
`{value, logs, jevCalls, storeWrites}`.

readme.section: The ptc capability (opt-in: the codemode tool)
readme.text:
- **Everything ships off**: `ptcEnabled: false` registers no tool;
  `jevEnabled: false` makes zero jev calls. Every jev call (failures included)
  appends one row to `<dsh home>/storages/ptc-subagent/usage.jsonl` (metadata
  and token counts only, never state text).
- **What comes with it**: the `ptc-subagent` opt-in template is the dedicated
  dispatch role; since 0.19.1 the bundle patch carries only the two guarded
  preset rows (`preset-native` / `preset-codemode`, disabled on profiles that
  select `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`) — the two service rows
  (`agent-preset-registry` / `subagent-model-selection-settings`) mount at
  runtime on the include tree instead, only where no same-id entry exists, so
  a profile that already mounts an agent-preset layer needs no manual
  de-duplication (issue #9, see docs/TROUBLESHOOTING-PRESET-ROWS.md).
- **Upgrading from the standalone ptc repo**: usage and config keys keep their
  names and meanings (the entry id becomes `dsh-subagent-registry`), the
  usage.jsonl path is unchanged, and existing records carry over.

The plugin ships a bundled skill named `dsh-subagent-registry-config`. Whenever the
conversation touches custom subagents, agent `.md` authoring, resume semantics,
or this plugin's configuration, dsh loads the bundled usage & configuration
guide, so the model can write agent files for you (collecting choices via
`ask_user_question`) and adjust the plugin config without digging through the
README. The skill is versioned and published with the package
(`skills/dsh-subagent-registry-config/SKILL.md`, plus an English `SKILL.en.md`
and a Russian `SKILL.ru.md` selected by the `language` key — see the table above).

**Requires dsh >= 0.2.0-rc.2** (the RC/stable line; the alpha line is not supported). Compatibility validated through `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.1-rc.2`. The host must mount session persistence and `sessionQuery`. Resume and follow-ups use each host's own session format; cross-version migration is not provided.

Option A — mount a checkout into a dsh profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile tui add ~/github/dsh-subagent-registry
```

Option B — npm dependency: `npm i @aiwayds/dsh-subagent-registry`, then load
the plugin under the stable id `dsh-subagent-registry` in your profile's
config, or mount it through a bundle patch (see `cordis.patch.yml` in this
repo for the pattern).

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> remove @aiwayds/dsh-subagent-registry
```

The host splices the plugin out of the profile; restart dsh and the
`use_agent` / `ask_agent` tools are gone. **Your agent files in
`~/.dsh/agents/` stay** — they are user-owned and never re-seeded or
overwritten. dsh-tui-pi degrades gracefully without this plugin (you just
lose custom-agent dispatch).

```sh
npm run check    # tsc --noEmit
npm run build    # tsc -> lib/
npm test         # unit regressions and real npm install in a temporary directory (no LLM)
npm run test:host # current SDK's real services/persistence/manager/spawn; scripted model, no network

Prepare isolated SDKs from the plugin directory (reuse existing closures when available):

```sh
npm install --prefix ../../.tmp/dsh-type-closure-rc2 --ignore-scripts @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query@0.2.0-rc.2
npm install --prefix ../../.tmp/dsh-type-closure --ignore-scripts @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.2 @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query@0.2.1-rc.2 @deepseek-ai/dsh-working-directory@0.2.1-rc.2
```

Override `DSH_TEST_RC2_CLOSURE_DIR` / `DSH_TEST_021_CLOSURE_DIR` with other isolated `node_modules` directories. Only model responses are scripted; host services and persistence use their actual published implementations.

This repo declares the `@deepseek-ai/*` packages (`cordis`, `dsh-subagent`,
`dsh-llm`, `schemastery`, …) as **optional peerDependencies** in releases
(`>=0.2.0-rc.2 || >=0.2.1-rc.1`). That is a deliberate two-layer split:

- **Release semantics (for consumers)**: the declaration says "use the host's
  own copies, range `>=0.2.0-rc.2 || >=0.2.1-rc.1`". Optional peers are never auto-installed
  by pnpm or npm, so they cannot materialize a second copy in the profile's
  `node_modules` that shadows the host's bundled closure. What does break
  hosts is a hard dependency pinned to an old rc — that can render a 0.2.x
  host unbootable (a known community failure mode).
- **Dev typecheck (for this repo)**: devDependencies pin the newer SDK;
  `scripts/link-dsh-closure.mjs` (postinstall) symlinks
  `node_modules/@deepseek-ai/*` to `DSH_CLOSURE_DIR` or the global dsh install's closure, keeping
  exactly one `@deepseek-ai/cordis` in the type graph — a second copy breaks
  the cordis `declare module` augmentation (`Property 'settings' does not
  exist on type 'Context'`).

Maintenance rule: keep these entries as optional peers — never move them back
to dependencies/devDependencies, and never drop `optional: true` (a
non-optional peer is auto-installed under pnpm's `auto-install-peers` and the
second-copy breakage returns). Likewise never add a hard dependency on any of
them: a pinned second copy shadows the host's bundled closure just the same.

`e2e/podman-install/` installs the **published** tarballs of this plugin, dsh-dcp, dsh-cron, dsh-llm-proxy, and dsh-profile-switch inside a container with a real dsh CLI, using a real npm client with dependency lifecycle scripts on — the exact intersection that let the packaged-`postinstall` breakage (#2) ship unnoticed. It asserts the install exits clean, the closure linker stands down in the consumer tree, the real host composes and boots each profile, and dcp's schema default + explicit-empty semantics survive the real config layer.

- Local (macOS, podman machine up): `e2e/podman-install/run.sh`
- The same assertions run bare on Linux (no podman needed) via the weekly scheduled `e2e install` workflow; `bash e2e/podman-install/entry.sh` works on any node 22+ machine with the global dsh CLI.
